title: Aseptic Technique

references.label: Biosafety in Microbiological and Biomedical Laboratories (BMBL)

summary: A set of practices used to prevent contamination of cultures, media, and reagents by unwanted microorganisms, and to protect the handler from exposure.
explanation: Aseptic technique includes working near a flame or in laminar airflow, flaming loops before and after use, minimizing time lids/caps are open, working quickly but not carelessly, and disinfecting work surfaces before and after use. It is a practice, not a single step, and applies throughout a procedure rather than at one point in it.
commonMisconceptions: That flaming a loop alone is 'doing aseptic technique' — it is one component among several.
That aseptic technique is only about protecting the worker — it equally protects the culture from contamination.
